title: ZAP, OWASP, and Checkmarx
description: What the ZAP project's own pages say about leaving OWASP in 2023 and about current ownership.
narrative:
An announcement in August 2023 indicates that ZAP was joining the Software Security Project, which it describes as a brand new initiative of the Linux Foundation, as one of its founding projects. A project can sit in only one foundation, so ZAP would leave OWASP. The same announcement says that Simon Bennetts had applied for ZAP to join OWASP soon after the 2010 launch, that leaving had first been raised in 2015, and that the team had signed an open letter to the OWASP Board earlier that year.

Related changes followed. The name became simply "ZAP", Docker Hub images moved to a new organisation, and for the first time two people would be supported full time: Simon and Ricardo.

In September 2024 a further announcement said Checkmarx would employ all three project leaders, and that the project would be known as "ZAP by Checkmarx". The project leaders were clear about what stayed the same: control remained with the ZAP Core Team, the code stayed open source under Apache v2, and the change gave the project proper backing, which the announcement called the first time in its history.

The project's own ownership page now describes ZAP as an independent open source project, controlled by the ZAP Core Team and supported by Checkmarx.

chapters.title: Leaving OWASP for the Software Security Project, August 2023
chapters.text: The post "ZAP is Joining the Software Security Project" (2023-08-01, Simon Bennetts) announces that ZAP is joining the SSP, "a brand new initiative of the Linux Foundation", as a founding project, and that "ZAP can only be in one foundation, so regretfully ZAP will be leaving OWASP." It says Simon applied for ZAP to join OWASP shortly after its launch in 2010, that leaving was first floated in 2015, that he raised the concern in his 2022 Global AppSec keynote, and that the ZAP team signed the Open Letter to the OWASP Board in February 2023. The practical changes it lists: the name loses its OWASP prefix and the project is "known as just "ZAP"", Docker Hub images move to a new organisation, and the GitHub Container Registry images are not affected. It also says SSP would support Simon and Ricardo (thc202) full time: "For the first time ever we have two people working on ZAP full-time and that will increase over time." The page now carries a banner saying ZAP is supported by Checkmarx and is not part of any foundation.

evidence.label: ZAP is Joining the Software Security Project

chapters.title: No longer an OWASP project
chapters.text: The ZAP project states that "ZAP is no longer an OWASP project, and has not been one since August 2023", and that the correct name is "ZAP" or "ZAP by Checkmarx".

evidence.label: ZAP: no longer an OWASP project

chapters.title: Checkmarx, September 2024
chapters.text: The post "ZAP Has Joined Forces With Checkmarx" (2024-09-24) says Checkmarx will employ all three ZAP project leaders (Simon, Ricardo and Rick), working on ZAP and on Checkmarx's DAST solution built on it, and that ZAP will be known as "ZAP by Checkmarx". It states what stays the same: "ZAP will stay under the control of the ZAP Core Team, remain open source, and stay licensed under Apache v2." It gives as the most important change "proper backing - for the first time in its history", and thanks CrashOverride, who "stepped up and supported us" earlier: "Without their help and support the ZAP project may not have survived."

evidence.label: ZAP Has Joined Forces With Checkmarx

chapters.title: Who runs ZAP now
chapters.text: The ownership page describes ZAP as "an independent Open Source project controlled by the ZAP Core Team and supported by Checkmarx". It links a post titled "ZAP Has Joined Forces With Checkmarx" (URL dated 2024-09-24).
